unsupported_claims: The AI claims second-order proximity is typically measured via dot product, cosine, or Jaccard-style overlap of neighborhood vectors, which the evidence does not specify (it only says the proximity is determined by the similarity between p_u and p_v without naming a measure).

The AI describes the measure as based on in-neighbor and out-neighbor sets separately, whereas the evidence defines it over the first-order proximity vectors of all vertices, not explicitly distinguishing in- and out-neighbors.
The AI's claim that the value is 0 in the no-shared-neighbor case is supported, so it is not listed here.
rationale: The core answer that second-order proximity is 0 when no vertex is linked from/to both vertices is directly supported by the evidence. However, the AI adds unsupported specifics about the similarity measures (dot product, cosine, Jaccard) and an in/out-neighbor framing that the passage does not state, and it fails to note that the papers do not describe any alternative handling beyond the zero case.
